objective: A GuardDuty finding of severity 4 or more (Medium, High and Critical) in fanwire-workload is emailed through the existing AlarmTopic, by one same-account EventBridge rule on the default event bus whose only target is that topic.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: this spec's Director PR has merged into outstanding-track-3-followups, and the branch is cut from an outstanding-track-3-followups that holds it.
Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation. They fail today because Fanwire-Messaging has no rule whose pattern names detail-type "GuardDuty Finding".

Fanwire-Messaging adds exactly one AWS::Events::Rule with logical id prefix GuardDutyFindingRule, on the default event bus (no EventBusName property), State ENABLED, whose EventPattern equals {"source": ["aws.guardduty"], "detail-type": ["GuardDuty Finding"], "detail": {"severity": [{"numeric": [">=", 4]}]}}. A test asserts that exact pattern.

The rule has exactly one target: Arn is the AlarmTopic's Ref, no RoleArn, and an InputTransformer whose InputPathsMap reads $.detail.severity, $.detail.type, $.detail.title, $.account, $.region and $.detail.id, and whose InputTemplate contains each of those six placeholders and the word GuardDuty. A test asserts the target.

The AlarmTopic's AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy gains one statement, Sid AllowEventBridgeGuardDutyFindings: Effect Allow, Principal Service events.amazonaws.com, Action sns:Publish, Resource the AlarmTopic's Ref, Condition ArnEquals aws:SourceArn = the rule's Arn (Fn::GetAtt). A test asserts it, and asserts AllowCloudWatchAlarms is unchanged.
No statement in the topic policy grants sns:Publish to events.amazonaws.com without that aws:SourceArn condition (the stock targets.SnsTopic grant has none, so it is not used). A test asserts it.
EXPECTED_ALARM_COUNT in infra/test/alarms.test.ts stays 25: a rule is not a CloudWatch alarm.
The existing MalwareScanResultRule and NotificationRule, their targets and the queue policies are unchanged.
The IAM gate (infra/test/iam-policy.test.ts) passes in every domain mode with no new ALLOW_LIST entry. infra/iam/** is unchanged: the CloudFormation execution role already holds events:* and sns:*.

The PR body carries the expected cdk diff: Fanwire-Messaging only, one AWS::Events::Rule added and the alarm topic's AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy modified. No other stack changes; no resource removed or replaced.

The PR body's manual steps, after the deploy: the human creates one sample finding of one High type in the workload detector 62d0584d4d193d4f24a7a4a5f375baa2 (aws guardduty create-sample-findings --finding-types UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/TorClient, never without --finding-types, which creates one of every type), and an email reaches the alarm topic's subscriber within 15 minutes. It names the rollback: if create-sample-findings is refused or no email arrives while the rule's TriggeredRules metric stays 0, the rule is removed in a follow-up PR and the finding recorded in the inventory.
npm run build, npm run lint, npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 and npm run synth pass in infra/. Nobody runs cdk deploy.

wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x00a-architecture-infra.md's "Alarms" section names the GuardDuty findings rule, its severity floor of 4, that it emails through the same topic, and that it is not counted in EXPECTED_ALARM_COUNT.
